title: Pre-Anesthesia Checklist & Fasting
sources: Critical Vector — Anesthesia Reference: Pre-Induction Checklist (MSMAID) + NPO Guidelines
Gelb AW et al. WHO-WFSA International Standards for a Safe Practice of Anesthesia. Anesthesiology 2018; ASA 2023 fasting guidelines; SPAQI 2025 GLP-1 update

changelog.change: Initial entry — the MSMAID pre-induction check and the ASA 2023 fasting intervals, including the GLP-1 agonist and carbohydrate-loading guidance.

summary: MSMAID before every induction: Machine · Suction · Monitors · Airway · IV · Drugs. ASA 2023 fasting: clear liquids 2 h, breast milk 4 h, formula 6 h, light meal 6 h, fatty/full meal 8 h. GI symptoms on a GLP-1 agonist → treat as a full stomach regardless of the fast.

rows: Full anaesthesia-machine check (APSF protocol). Backup ventilation (self-inflating bag) + an O₂ source confirmed accessible.

SpO₂, NIBP, ECG, EtCO₂, temperature as standard. Adjuncts per case: arterial line, processed-EEG, and a QUANTITATIVE neuromuscular monitor (strongly recommended, ASA 2023) — calibrate before induction.
Primary AND backup plan confirmed. Mask, ETT / LMA, video + direct laryngoscope, bougie, stylet, tape. Optimise position (sniffing / ramp).
Adequate gauge / number / flow confirmed; lines flushed and labelled.

Induction agents drawn and labelled (ASTM colour code). Emergency drugs accessible: epinephrine, atropine, succinylcholine, a vasopressor (phenylephrine / ephedrine), and lipid emulsion if a block is planned. Know who to call for help.
Water, pulp-free juice, black coffee, clear tea, carbonated drinks. Carbohydrate-containing clear drinks (maltodextrin, sports drinks) are included — reduce hunger/thirst, no added aspiration risk
Toast + a clear liquid = a light meal
ASA 2023 — no increased aspiration risk; ask the patient to spit it out and not swallow excess saliva

body.text: GLP-1 receptor agonists (semaglutide, tirzepatide, liraglutide) slow gastric emptying. ASA 2023: hold a daily agent for 1 day, a weekly agent for 1 week, before an elective procedure, plus standard fasting. SPAQI 2025 update: if the patient has ANY GI symptoms (nausea, vomiting, bloating, abdominal distension), treat as a full stomach regardless of the hold or fast — consider gastric POCUS pre-op, and use RSI / awake technique / regional as appropriate. Holding the drug does not by itself remove the aspiration risk, and stopping it can worsen glycaemic control — individualise with endocrinology.
Carbohydrate loading (ASA 2023, ERAS-endorsed): a clear carbohydrate drink (~50 g CHO) up to 2 h pre-op reduces insulin resistance, PONV, and anxiety — appropriate for elective non-diabetic adults.

buildNote: Tier 3, low churn. MSMAID could also be a Procedures workflow node. The full WHO surgical safety checklist (sign-in / time-out / sign-out) is a separate module.
